course13.title: Basic Grammar Essentials
course13.description: Subject pronouns and the verbs ‘essere’ (to be) and ‘avere’ (to have). Build simple sentences. Paired items are split into separate lessons. Step 3 only uses vocabulary from earlier courses or this course.

step1.note: EE-oh — Subject pronoun; often dropped in Italian.

questions.prompt: Select the word for 'I'
What does this mean in English: Io
Select the word for 'You (singular, informal)'
What does this mean in English: Tu
Select the word for 'He'
What does this mean in English: Lui
Select the word for 'She'
What does this mean in English: Lei

step1.note: Formal ‘you’. Capitalize ‘Lei’ in writing; context distinguishes it from ‘she’.
VOY — Addressing more than one person.

step1.note: Subject pronoun can be dropped: (Io) sono di Milano.

mcq.question: Which phrase means 'I am from Milan'?

step2.type_prompt: S__o di M____o  = I am from Milan

mcq.question: Which phrase means 'We have a car'?

step2.type_prompt: A_____o u_a m______a  = We have a car

mcq.question: Which phrase means 'There is a problem'?

step2.type_prompt: C'è un p______a  = There is a problem

mcq.question: Which phrase means 'There are two problems'?

step2.type_prompt: Ci s__o d_e p______i  = There are two problems
